raw_review_excerpt:
The research document is well-structured, the upstream-first overlay strategy is sound, and the prior peer-review concerns have been substantively addressed. For the narrow question — is Phase 1 ready to proceed? — the answer is yes. Phase 1 is a doc-only, fully reversible branch creation from upstream-main that carries no installer, identity, or history-rewrite risk. The hardened Phase 1 validation block now includes AGENTS.md composition, doc path verification, marker schema check, remote topology, and rollback tag availability — all of which were missing in the prior round. The remaining open decisions (minimal profile, Codex hooks, marker migration) are correctly scoped to Phases 2–5 and do not gate Phase 1.

Issues:
- 1. [NOTE] Phase 1 deliverable list contains two micro-decisions in 'or' form
- 2. [NOTE] Mase review notes vs decision-section status labels are not reconciled
- 3. [WARN] Phase 2 marker migration for existing installs is named but not yet designed

issues.title: Phase 1 deliverable list contains two micro-decisions in 'or' form
issues.details: Phase 1 says to re-add 'OSS fork marker or updated equivalent' and 'fork propagation skill or a pointer to my-oss-fork-manager'. The 'or' means the implementer must make two small decisions during Phase 1 without pre-agreed defaults. Both are low-risk, but undecided items in a phase spec create unnecessary ambiguity during execution.
issues.suggested_fix: Resolve both before starting Phase 1: (1) keep .codex/oss-fork-manager.json as-is since the global manager still expects schema_version 1, and (2) add a docs pointer to my-oss-fork-manager rather than porting the full repo-local propagation skill, since Phase 2 will bring the scripts anyway.

issues.title: Mase review notes vs decision-section status labels are not reconciled
issues.details: The review-notes table says plan-brief is 'Drop' and hooks.json is 'Move to upstream', but the corresponding decision sections still carry 'Decision needed' headers for adjacent items (minimal profile, Codex update hook). The doc never explicitly declares which provisional directions are now binding vs. still exploratory. This is cosmetic for Phase 1 but will create confusion when Phases 3–5 start.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a one-line status annotation to each decision section header: 'Decided: [direction]' or 'Open: awaiting [specific input]'. This can be done during Phase 1 doc cleanup or as a pre-Phase-3 gate.

issues.title: Phase 2 marker migration for existing installs is named but not yet designed
issues.details: The peer review follow-up table marks existing fork-managed installs as an 'Open migration item' and the document says Phase 2 'must explicitly handle marker/identity migration for existing installs.' However, the Phase 2 section only adds 'support old marker identity fields during transition' without specifying the migration behavior (rewrite markers in place? dual-read? migration script?). This is correctly deferred from Phase 1 but needs design before Phase 2 starts.
issues.suggested_fix: Before starting Phase 2, define the concrete migration behavior: whether inventory/propagation will dual-read old and new marker schemas, whether markers are rewritten during propagation apply, and what happens to the two known stale installs (global Codex, my-second-brain-build).

Resolution criteria for the three remaining open decisions (minimal profile, Codex update hook, repo-local agent guardrails) are not defined
recommended_fixes: Resolve the two 'or' micro-decisions in Phase 1 deliverable list before starting implementation

review.best_case: Phase 1 is narrow, reversible, and doc-only: create a branch from upstream-main and re-add Mase guardrail docs, fork marker, and AGENTS.md overlay. The hardened validation block now includes 5 concrete checks beyond git diff --check (AGENTS.md composition, doc path validity, marker schema, remote topology, rollback tag). All prior peer-review concerns are either resolved in the current artifact or correctly deferred to later phases. The open decisions (minimal profile, Codex hooks, marker migration) are appropriately gated to Phases 2–5 and do not block the doc-only foundation phase. If Phase 1 lands cleanly, it establishes the upstream-first baseline that all subsequent phases build on, with the rollback tag verified as a recovery anchor.
strongest_objections: The strongest remaining concern is that Phase 2 marker migration is named but not designed. The document correctly says 'Phase 2 must explicitly handle marker/identity migration for existing installs' and names two known stale installs, but the Phase 2 section only says 'support old marker identity fields during transition' without specifying the mechanism. This is not a Phase 1 blocker but could stall Phase 2 if not addressed before it starts.

The upstream AGENTS.md composition check is scoped as a Phase 1 validation task, meaning it will be discovered during execution rather than pre-resolved. The follow-up table notes upstream AGENTS.md 'still describes SDK-era structure in places, so fork overlay must compose carefully.' If the composition turns out to be complex, it could expand Phase 1 scope beyond what was planned.

Three open decisions (minimal profile, Codex update hook, repo-local agents) have no stated resolution criteria or deadlines. This doesn't block Phase 1, but it means Phases 3–4 could stall waiting for Mase input if the decisions aren't teed up in advance.
hidden_assumptions: Phase 1 assumes the upstream AGENTS.md composition will be straightforward enough to handle within the doc-only phase scope — the follow-up table flags SDK-era drift but doesn't estimate composition complexity
The document assumes Mase's provisional directions are stable enough to build Phase 1 on, though they are explicitly labeled as directional rather than binding
Phase 1 assumes the oss-fork-manager.json marker can be carried forward as-is, based on current schema_version 1 match — if the global manager evolves before Phase 2, this may need revisiting

The phased approach assumes upstream won't push breaking changes that invalidate the overlay during implementation — acceptable for Phase 1 since it's fast and doc-only, but a real risk for the multi-week Phases 2–6 campaign
review.what_would_change_my_mind: I would downgrade to mixed if Phase 1 itself had an unresolved dependency — for example, if the upstream AGENTS.md composition turned out to require installer or code changes rather than just doc composition, or if the oss-fork-manager marker schema had changed since the follow-up verification. Neither of these is indicated by current evidence. I would also downgrade if someone showed that one of the Phase 1 deliverables depends on an open decision (minimal profile, hooks, etc.) — but inspection confirms Phase 1 only touches docs, guardrails, and the existing marker, none of which depend on those decisions.
next_checks: During Phase 1 execution: compose the fork AGENTS.md overlay against upstream's current AGENTS.md and verify they're coherent (this is the one remaining validation task that hasn't been pre-resolved)
During Phase 1 execution: verify all doc references (script paths, branch names, remote URLs) point to paths that exist on the upstream-main tree
Before Phase 2: inspect the exact marker schemas of the two known stale installs to determine migration requirements
Before Phase 3: tee up the minimal profile decision with a concrete recommendation so Phase 3 doesn't stall on input
